a:r.a:t: Internet culture inspires a rise in offbeat humour, design and collaboration​

Digital natives are rapidly adopting and remixing new forms of self expression. Accustomed to identity-building and socialising online, younger generations – Gen Z in particular – are pioneers of internet communication, mixing and matching various cultural cues, channels and genres to create highly visual messaging. They might share trending memes on Instagram one minute, watch cinematic deepfakes on YouTube the next, and then check in on a colourful TikTok personality. Their influence on culture more widely means that the absurdist, self-referential tone of once-niche internet culture is now in common use.​

Weirdness is an aspirational identity trait. This is especially true online; we see this in the idiosyncratic nature of subcultures found on TikTok such as E-Girls and WitchTok, which are far less polished than the Millennial Instagram aesthetic, and celebrate that fact. But offbeat humour and aesthetics, even ugly design, are also a result of this trend. In a bid to be relatable and court virality, brands are embracing weirdness and irreverence through counterintuitive collaborations, playfully odd product design, liberal use of internet speak, and references to niche memes and subcultures. ​

The challenge for brands is to keep up with the pace. Memes, tongue-in-cheek humour and irony are increasingly part of brands’ vernacular. The rulebook for what constitutes effective messaging is being rewritten as brands look to appeal to digital natives, and as young generations become accustomed to communicating with brands like they do with friends. But meme culture is constantly evolving. From still image memes to animated gifs to video clips with embedded sound and text, internet humour doesn’t sit still. In fact, memes by nature are often random and fleeting; they represent a shared experience that make viewers feel part of a club, if only for a brief moment. The savviest brands are those that engage with cultural moments in a timely and authentic way, grabbing attention just long enough to connect with their audience and demonstrate relevance.
